ca_troubled_waters_boulder.blurb: A large boulder beside Pyramid Creek in the Gemini Boulders, up the canyon from Highway 50 near Strawberry and above 6,500 feet. Eleven problems share the block, most of them easy, in the V0 to V2 range, with a handful of harder lines up to about V7. Some lines finish over water, so landings can be wet and a pad needs care. The north side still holds unclimbed possibilities. It is a good stop for a mixed-ability group after the hike in, and it doubles as the landmark for the other blocks nearby.
ca_troubled_waters_boulder.approach: Follow the Horsetail Falls trail on foot for around 40 minutes to the obvious big boulder beside the creek. If you reach the falls themselves, you have gone a few minutes too far.

ca_masters_of_the_universe.blurb: A small cluster of boulders on Mount Woodson in northern San Diego County, a little over 1,900 feet up and east of the Tower One area. Mostly it is pure bouldering, nine problems that run from moderate around V3 to quite hard, including a few at the double-digit end, plus two short trad lines at 5.10 and 5.11. Power lines pass overhead. It makes an easy add-on to a day on the wider Woodson boulder fields rather than a destination of its own.

ca_hamburger_crack_area.blurb: A compact roadside stop on Mount Woodson in northern San Diego County, sitting just before the Poison Oak Crack area. Eleven climbs mix mostly boulder problems, from easy up to a very hard V12, with two trad lines, one short sport route and a top-rope. Three of the lead routes sit around 5.10. Boulders next to the pavement have steep ground beneath them, so spot the landing carefully. The area is small and quick to tick off alongside neighbouring sections.

ca_slide_wall.blurb: A steep, north-facing slab wall in the Benches section of the Emeralds, near the South Yuba River off Bowman Lake Road in the Tahoe area. Eleven routes, mostly bolted, with two trad lines, run from easy 5.6 and 5.7 up to around 5.11. Holds are crimpy, and the newer lines left of the hardest route are juggy and moderate, which suits newer leaders on busy weekends. Big stacked blocks sit at the base. The wall still needs traffic to clean up, and poison oak grows nearby.

ca_space_wall.blurb: An east-facing wall of weathered granite on Donner Summit, with a view across Donner Lake. Eleven routes, mostly long, well-protected sport lines with a few trad and top-rope options, mainly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range with a single 5.9 and one very hard 5.13 line. The climbing is high quality and moderately challenging, and the wall feels more secluded than the roadside rock nearby. The walk in is short, but it finishes with a class 3 downclimb to the base.
